description: This grouped bar chart illustrates the number of datasets published per year, categorized by language. The horizontal category axis is labeled "Year" and displays chronological years from 2012 to 2022. The vertical value axis is labeled "Number of datasets" and uses a logarithmic scale (base 10) ranging from $10^0$ to $10^2$, with major tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at $10^0$, $10^1$, and $10^2$. The bars are grouped by year, with each group containing up to six adjacent bars representing different language categories as defined in the legend titled "Language". The legend maps colors to categories: blue corresponds to a blurred label, orange to "All other", green to "Arabic", red to "Bengali", purple to "Spanish", and brown to "Russian". In the early years from 2012 to 2015, only the blue bars are present, representing approximately 2 to 3 datasets each year. The number of categories and the height of the bars generally increase over time, with the tallest bar being the blue bar in 2021, reaching nearly $10^2$ (approximately 90 datasets), closely followed by the blue and orange bars in 2020. The shortest bars represent a value of $10^0$ (1 dataset), seen for the red category in 2017 and 2018, and the brown category in 2022. The groups are sorted chronologically on the horizontal axis, and within each year, the bars follow the order presented in the legend. Notably, the bars for the year 2022 are visually distinguished by being rendered in faded, lighter shades of their respective category colors.
